St. Andrew Rublev

Saints

Saint Andrew Rublev

St. Andrei Rublev · St. Andrey Rublev · St. Andrej Rublëv · St. Andrew Rublev the Iconographer

Period
Born c. 1360–1370; died c. 1427–1430
Region
Moscow; Vladimir; Trinity Monastery, Russia
Titles / vocation
Monastic · Iconographer
Commemoration
July 4

Introduction

Saint Andrew Rublev was a Russian monk and iconographer, remembered especially for the Trinity icon and for work in Moscow, Vladimir, and the Trinity Monastery.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeath and martyrdomWritings and legacyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Monastic repose, approximately 1427–1430; exact date uncertain

Read circumstances and sources

Background

The OCA places his birth near Moscow between 1360 and 1370. Its life connects his early formation with the Trinity Monastery. He later moved to the Andronikov Monastery, where he became a monk.

[1] Published ecclesiastical biography / commemoration · Opening two paragraphs: approximate birth and monastic formation

Life and notable events

Chronicles first name him in 1405 among painters decorating Moscow’s Annunciation Cathedral. In 1408 he worked with another monk on Vladimir’s Dormition Cathedral. He also helped adorn the rebuilt church of the Trinity Monastery after its destruction by the Tatars.

[1] Published ecclesiastical biography / commemoration · Paragraphs on chronicles, Annunciation Cathedral, Vladimir and Trinity Monastery

Death and martyrdom

The cited life dates Saint Andrew’s death between 1427 and 1430 and places his burial at the Andronikov Monastery. It records a monk’s repose rather than martyrdom; an exact death date is not established here.

[1] Published ecclesiastical biography / commemoration · Final paragraph: death range and burial

Writings and legacy

His best-known icon is the Trinity, based on the Hospitality of Abraham. His principal legacy in this account is iconography: images created within the worship and monastic life of the Church, rather than a body of theological prose.

[1] Published ecclesiastical biography / commemoration · Paragraph on the Holy Trinity icon
